label: NEW PATTERNS

cover.headline: Why *your own life* makes a marriage stronger

points.heading: Your friendships
points.body: Friends give you support, perspective, and a place to just be you.
points.panel: Text one friend you’ve been meaning to see.

points.heading: Your interests
points.body: Something you love doing, just for the joy of it.
points.panel: “What did I love doing before life got so busy?”

points.heading: Your quiet time
points.body: A little time alone helps you come back calmer.
points.panel: “I’m taking an hour for myself on Saturday morning.”

points.heading: Your own opinions
points.body: Closeness doesn’t mean agreeing on everything.
points.panel: “I see it differently, and that’s okay.”

points.heading: Your own growth
points.body: Learning and changing keep you interesting, to yourself first.
points.panel: Start one small thing you’re curious about this month.

caption:
It can feel like a strong marriage means doing everything together. But two people who each have a full life often have more to bring to each other.

Keeping your own friendships, interests, and quiet time isn’t selfish. It’s part of staying yourself inside a relationship.

Save this as a reminder, and follow @spotseason for more.
